reviews.text:
One Star: I’m Looking for Someone’s Story, Not Their Advertising Campaign

I joined OkCupid hoping to find genuine companionship with someone reasonably close to home.

Instead, I received introductions from women living on other continents while the app displayed approximately 83 likes or interested profiles and encouraged me to pay $39.99 to see who they were.

Why should I pay to discover whether those people even live in my country, much less within driving distance?

I’m looking for real conversations with real people, not a collection of glamorous photographs, questionable matches, and subscription prompts.

My experience has been frustrating, disappointing, and discouraging.

OkCupid, you missed out on a customer who was genuinely interested in finding a meaningful relationship. Willing to pay if you didn’t spam my like box with women from other continents.

reviews.title: More Time Dealing With Scammers Than Meeting People
reviews.text:
I’m paying for an OkCupid subscription, yet much of my experience has involved identifying and dealing with suspicious profiles rather than meeting genuine people.

Today alone, I encountered two women whose conversations followed remarkably similar patterns. Both claimed to be auditors, gave vague responses, and seemed more interested in moving our conversations to other messaging apps than actually getting acquainted. When I questioned their authenticity, both disappeared.

Then, approximately ten minutes later, I suddenly lost access to my paid account.

OkCupid no longer recognizes my phone number or my email and password. I’ve attempted to reset my password multiple times, but no reset email arrives, including in my spam folder.

I can’t prove these events are connected, but the timing is certainly concerning.

I’m paying for a dating service, yet I’m spending more time screening suspicious accounts than having meaningful conversations. Now I can’t even access the service I’m paying for.

OkCupid needs to do a better job protecting legitimate users, investigating suspicious accounts, and providing accessible support when paying members are unexpectedly locked out.

At this point, I’m extremely disappointed, both with the quality of the experience and the lack of account access.

reviews.title: Riddled with Fake Profiles
reviews.text:
OkCupid’s platform is riddled with suspicious, misleading, and potentially fake profiles, yet the company continues to charge users for access to its services. That is unacceptable.

People join dating platforms because they genuinely want to meet other people, build relationships, and establish meaningful connections. Instead, users are left questioning whether the people they are interacting with are real, whether profiles accurately represent the individuals behind them, and whether the service they are paying for delivers what it promises.

The audacity of charging customers for a service when there are serious concerns about the authenticity of the profiles on that platform is astounding. Users should not have to spend their time and money investigating whether the person on the other end of a conversation actually exists or is genuinely interested in meeting someone.

If OkCupid is aware that fake or deceptive profiles are a recurring problem and continues to collect membership fees without taking meaningful steps to address it, that raises serious questions about its priorities and its responsibility to paying customers.

I expect more than generic assurances. I expect OkCupid to explain what measures it takes to identify and remove fraudulent profiles, how it protects paying members from deceptive accounts, and what recourse is available when users pay for a service undermined by those accounts.

Dating is already difficult enough without having to navigate a platform

reviews.title: Misleading and frustrating subscription experience
reviews.text:
I would not recommend paying for OkCupid. Before subscribing, I was shown a very large number under “Interested in You,” which gave the impression that these were people who had actually liked my profile. After paying, I discovered that this section includes people who merely VIEWED my profile as well as people who actually liked me. Those are obviously not the same thing.

Even worse, once you subscribe, you’re repeatedly shown profiles of people who simply viewed you and apparently chose not to like you. I can’t understand why anyone would want to be bombarded with that information, and I found the experience unpleasant rather than useful.

Now I’m also seeing old likes being recycled. Profiles I already reviewed and swiped left on are appearing again as though they’re new, which makes the experience feel even more misleading.

I contacted customer support more than a week ago requesting a refund and explaining these issues, and I still have not received a response.

I paid because the numbers presented before subscribing made the service appear very different from what I actually received. I canceled my subscription and would never subscribe again or recommend this app.

In my experience, OKCupid is full of suspicious and potentially fake profiles. The pattern I encountered was extremely concerning: after matching, the person would try to move the conversation away from the app, first to Instagram, then Facebook, and eventually WhatsApp.
From there, the conversation would progress from small talk to requests for a face photo and personal information, including your full name and Facebook profile, followed by attempts to establish trust by asking you to confirm your identity/profile. The situation could then become sexual, with requests for intimate video calls or intimate photos. The person may then claim that they recorded the interaction and threaten to send it to your Facebook friends unless you comply with their demands.
There are also scams involving requests for screenshots of your bank account and instructions about moving or receiving money. I have not personally experienced that particular part, but I am aware that this is another tactic used in online dating scams.
Please be extremely careful. Don't move conversations off the dating app too quickly, don't send intimate photos or videos to people you don't know, don't share your full personal information or bank details, and never follow instructions from a stranger involving your money.
OKCupid needs to do much more to detect and remove fraudulent profiles and protect users from these types of scams. Based on what I experienced and observed, I cannot recommend this app.

reviews.title: 11 years on OkCupid. Here’s why it’s getting worse.
reviews.text:
Update 06/2026

Deleted the app from my devices. 

——

After the update 114.3.0

After updating the app, I checked Passport mode and the first 23 profiles shown were from Indonesia, Kenya, the Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia, Colombia, Taiwan, China and the US. I didn’t see a single profile from Europe, despite being based in London.

—

Update 05/2026

The developers have broken the compatibility feature.

I recently matched with someone who was supposedly 98% compatible with me. However, when I looked at our answers, I found that we agreed on only 28 questions, disagreed on 110, and had 25 unanswered. That means we agreed on only about 20% of the questions we had both answered, yet the app still claims we are a 98% match.

Years ago, OkCupid’s compatibility score made much more sense. It considered not only your answers, but also how important each question was to you, which answers you would accept from another person, and other weighting factors. Those options have now been removed. Today you can only select a single answer for each question, so there is far less information available to calculate compatibility. Yet the app still displays extremely high percentages that don’t reflect the actual level of agreement between users.

The compatibility score now feels inflated and misleading, making it much less useful than it used to be.

reviews.title: Shocking
reviews.text:
OKCupid shows you likes but doesn’t let you realistically act on them. I’ve had around 20 likes, no matches, no swipes left, and no meaningful way to engage unless I pay. Other apps at least let things happen organically — here it feels like interest is deliberately hidden to push premium.

The app creates frustration by limiting swipes while dangling likes you can’t see or reach. It doesn’t feel like dating, it feels like being teased into spending money. If someone likes you, you should actually be able to encounter them naturally through normal use, not be locked behind a paywall.

reviews.title: Bad
reviews.text: I made my account, set my location preference to 25 miles (I'm around 30-35 from London) and all it showed me are people who have their location set to London but say in their profile that they actually live in another country, typically Indonesia or Kenya. After dredging through at least a hundred of these (not exaggerating) and finding someone who's profile I actually wanted to leave a like on, the app glitched, wouldn't let me type anything, then crashed. It's done this multiple times, so I just can't like anyone's profile. I've tried restarting and stuff but it's not worked.

reviews.title: Do not download
reviews.text: The app is desperate for a review so here we go. Don’t do it. Don’t get this app. It’s terrible. Messages just stop being received after a while. You’ll be mid conversation, get a notification saying you have another message but there won’t be one there. This has happened to every conversation I’ve had on there that hasn’t moved elsewhere before the 5th or 6th message. I saw someone saying you need to buy the premium service to fix this. Nearly £40 a month for a basic feature like working messages? OkCupid needs binned.

reviews.title: An absolute joke
reviews.text:
3-4 days after downloading the app got locked out suddenly. Unable to log back in, tried changing the password, no links been received. Contacted the support, 3days later get somewhat automated vague response something regarding the ban? 
No further human contact. Not responding to emails ! I have Spent hours and hours answering the questionnaires, prefecting the profile talking to some people. I haven’t violated any rules to my knowledge and no one even tries to respond to my quieres in a decent manner! This is the first dating app i tried in over 10 years and my experience is just horrendous!

AVOID THE AUTOMATED BOTS
